TECH2_2021-41.exp: Self-service is the Business Model Canvas relationship type where the firm supplies the tools and the customer serves themselves with no direct human contact. Co-creation involves customers producing value with the firm, and 'personal' is the opposite, being assistance from a human representative.

TECH2_2021-42.exp: The Digital India programme's tagline is 'Power to Empower'. 'Transform India' belongs to the broader slogan of transforming India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy, which is the programme's vision statement rather than its motto.

TECH2_2021-43.exp: Digital India is built on exactly three vision areas: Digital Infrastructure as a Utility to Every Citizen, Governance and Services on Demand, and Digital Empowerment of Citizens. 'Technology Central to enable Change' is not one of them.

TECH2_2021-44.exp: Universal digital literacy sits squarely under Digital Empowerment of Citizens, along with digitally accessible resources, documents available on the cloud and content in Indian languages. Cashless transactions belong to Governance and Services on Demand, while CSC access and a secure cyberspace fall under Digital Infrastructure as a Utility.

TECH2_2021-45.exp: The CSC scheme is structured in three tiers: the VLE (Village Level Entrepreneur) running the centre, the SCA (Service Centre Agency) managing a cluster of centres, and the SDA (State Designated Agency) overseeing implementation in the state. SCD is not a CSC entity.

TECH2_2021-46.exp: DigiLocker allots each resident cloud storage linked to their Aadhaar number, which is also what authenticates the account and enables issuers to push documents into it. The other identifiers are not the linking key.

TECH2_2021-47.exp: The nine pillars include 'Information for All' and separately 'IT for Jobs', but there is no pillar called 'Information Technology for All'. Universal Access to Phones (mobile connectivity), Broadband Highways and Electronics Manufacturing are all genuine pillars, so the trap here is the near-miss renaming of 'Information for All'.

TECH2_2021-48.exp: Digital India was formally launched on 1 July 2015, although the Cabinet had approved the programme the previous year. Answering 2014 confuses approval with launch, which is the standard trap on this date.

TECH2_2021-49.exp: The National Digital Library of India was the NMEICT pilot that built a virtual repository of learning resources with a single-window search across sources. SWAYAM and MOOCs deliver courses rather than aggregate a repository.

TECH2_2021-50.exp: UMANG expands to Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance, the single app front-ending hundreds of central and state services. Option C is a plausible-looking invention built on forcing the letters NG.

TECH2_2021-51.exp: UPI, developed by NPCI, enables instant inter-account transfer using a virtual payment address so bank details need not be shared. IMPS, also from NPCI, predates UPI and does not use the virtual payment address, which is the distinguishing feature named in the question.

TECH2_2021-52.exp: Digitization converts records into electronic form that can be backed up and stored off-site, so a fire destroys no information. Fire equipment, fire-resistant rooms and photocopies all still leave a single physical location holding the only copies.

TECH2_2021-53.exp: The Digitize India Platform is built on crowdsourcing, so its stakeholders are the user organizations submitting scanned documents, the digital contributors who transcribe snippets, and the platform operators. The conventional data entry operator is precisely the role the crowdsourced model replaces.

TECH2_2021-54.exp: The Online Registration System (ORS) is the national portal that lets patients book OPD appointments in participating government hospitals, linked to Aadhaar. A hospital management system is internal administrative software, not a citizen-facing appointment service.

TECH2_2021-55.exp: Every enterprise architecture framework, whatever its notation, moves explicitly from the business layer (goals, processes, information) down to the technology layer, so the business-to-IT transition is the shared element. IT dictating business needs inverts the whole premise of enterprise architecture.

TECH2_2021-56.exp: Architecture is a design choice, not a mechanical derivation, so the same requirement set handed to different organisations yields different architectures shaped by their skills, constraints and preferences. Option C hedges the same point but the standard textbook statement is the definite one.

TECH2_2021-57.exp: Service Oriented Architecture is defined as a component-based architecture in which loosely coupled services communicate by message passing and are consumed by clients on demand. EBS and GEC are not architectural taxonomies of this kind.

TECH2_2021-58.exp: Viruses, worms and Trojan horses are all forms of malicious code, that is, programs written to damage or subvert a system. Client threats and communication channel threats classify where an attack strikes, not what these programs are.

TECH2_2021-59.exp: In the security engineering life cycle the security policy is derived from the security requirements and then drives the specification of the security infrastructure, so the policy stage sits between the two. This item is ambiguous because option D names essentially the same stage in activity form, and infrastructure implementation clearly comes later.

TECH2_2021-60.exp: eSAFE is the e-Governance Security Assurance Framework, the STQC-developed framework for assessing and certifying the security of e-governance applications. The other expansions substitute a single attribute for the assurance concept the framework is built around.
